title: Day 16 — Token-Bucket Rate Limiter
prompt: This token-bucket rate limiter has two bugs QA found: after an idle period it lets a burst through, and it rejects a request that needs exactly the tokens available. Walk me through the token math and the fixes.

clarifications.answer: Yes — after refilling, tokens must never exceed capacity. The idle burst is because refill isn't capped.
A request needing exactly the available tokens must succeed — the comparison should be >=, not >.
Refill = elapsed_seconds * refillPerSec, added to current tokens, then capped at capacity.
On rejection, don't consume tokens. (Refilling on that call is fine; just don't deduct cost.)
Time is passed in as a seconds value (injected), so there's no real clock in the logic — that's what makes it testable.
Tokens are fractional — 0.5s at 2/s yields 1 token. Don't floor them.

hints: Write the invariant first: 0 <= tokens <= capacity, always.
The idle-burst bug is a missing Math.min(capacity, ...) around the refill; the rejection bug is '>' where it should be '>='.
tokens = Math.min(capacity, tokens + elapsed * refillPerSec); then if (tokens >= cost) { tokens -= cost; return true; } return false;
